KEN.note: The document names no authentication, e-signature or PKI service.

facts.fact: PS Belio Kipsang told the National Assembly committee that development of a hospital e-notification system is complete and will be rolled out soon, relaying each birth to Civil Registration Services, which will issue the child a Unique Personal Identifier (Maisha Number) that becomes the national ID number at 18.
facts.system: e-notification system / Unique Personal Identifier generator

systems.owner: State Department for Immigration and Citizen Services

KEN.note: The e-notification is a hospital relay to the registrar; the document does not say the registrar's own register is a digital system in service or being rolled out.
No count or share of people holding a national ID is given.

facts.fact: PS Belio Kipsang said all children will be issued a Unique Personal Identifier (Maisha Number) at birth, kept for life and becoming the national ID card number at 18, through an e-notification system that is built and to be rolled out soon.

KEN.note: The document says nothing on who operates, maintains or owns the ID system.

facts.fact: The Nation says that at launch the Maisha number was meant to serve as the Personal Identification Number for Kenya Revenue Authority and the National Social Security Fund.

The Nation says the government rolled out the Maisha number, a unique personal number assigned to the Maisha Card, a third-generation digital ID card, and that registration was cleared to proceed in 2024 after a court challenge.

systems.owner: State Department for Immigration and Citizen Services

KEN.note: A future system number 'existing in the national population register' is mentioned only in passing; no register is stated as built or in service.
The e-notification is hospital notification to the registrar, class notification, noted and not assessed.
